item.title: Hong Kong to see 11.38 million inbound and outbound trips during Lunar New Year holiday period
item.description: Hong Kong is expected to see around 11.38 million trips made in and out of the city during the upcoming Lunar New Year holiday period, the Immigration Department has said. item.title: Hong Kong’s CK Hutchison warns of legal action if Danish firm Maersk takes over Panama ports
item.description: Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison has warned it will take legal action if Danish shipping giant AP Møller-Maersk takes over the operation of two ports on the Panama Canal run by its subsidiary. item.title: China cracks down on anti-marriage social media content during Lunar New Year holiday
item.description: China’s top internet regulator said on Thursday it would launch a crackdown during the Lunar New Year holiday period to curb social media content it deemed problematic including any that fanned fears about getting married or having children. item.title: Japan seizes Chinese fishing vessel, arrests captain
item.description: Japan seized a Chinese fishing boat and arrested its skipper, authorities said Friday, an incident that could deepen a spat between the Asian giants. item.title: Hong Kong may roll out renewal-based certification regime for teachers in 2027, with nat. security stipulations
item.description: Hong Kong has proposed a new certification regime for teachers at publicly-funded or international schools, which would require renewal every three years. item.title: Rehousing plan for Tai Po fire victims coming in ‘near term,’ says leader John Lee as another patient discharged
item.description: Chief Executive John Lee says he will announce rehousing plans for victims displaced by the Tai Po fire “in the near term,” adding that he has ordered the taskforce overseeing resettlement to work “non-stop” over the Lunar New Year break. item.title: Hong Kong’s cash-strapped flagship arts district inks HK$3 billion loan with partially state-owned bank

item.title: Student who launched petition urging probe into deadly Tai Po fire says CUHK expelled him weeks before graduation
item.description: A Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) student who launched a now-removed petition calling for government accountability following November’s deadly Tai Po fire has said he has been expelled. item.title: Beijing vows ‘measures’ after CIA Chinese-language recruitment ad
item.description: Beijing will take “all necessary measures” against foreign espionage activities, the foreign ministry said Friday, after the US spy agency issued a recruitment video targeting Chinese military personnel.
